Notes: ROUND AN (Anthony, 10 Oct: look A, THE CLUB NOTICEBOARD). EVERY PIECE OF THE DORMS SCREEN: its picture, where it goes and how big. THE ROOM TABS: one pennant per room, hanging from a string. X and Y are the first pennant's top-left, as a share of the screen (0 = left / top, 1 = right / bottom). SCALE = screen pixels per picture pixel. STEP = the gap from one pennant to the next, as a share of the screen's width - ten rooms need ten pennants, so keep Step x 10 short of the notice board.
How much LOWER the pennant of the room you are in hangs, as a share of the screen's height.
Where the room number sits in the pennant: the middle of its cream circle, as a share of the PENNANT picture.
The one line on the wall (ROOM 1 - 8 asleep - 10 of 10 beds), top-left, as a share of the screen. The explaining is the Head Coach's: Guide.csv dorms_explain, DormsDialogue.csv.
THE SHOP: the club's notice board, top-left as a share of the screen. Keep it on the wall, above the beds (DormBeds.csv) - it must never cover one. The pieces below sit ON it.
The folded camp bed: click to buy a single bed (Tuning.csv dorm_bed_price). X and Y are its MIDDLE, as a share of the BOARD.
The door key: click to buy the next room (Dorms.csv). Hover it for every room's price. Middle, as a share of the board.
The price card picture, pinned under each thing. It stretches to fit its words.
The bed's price card: X = its middle, Y = its top, as shares of the board.
The room's price card, the same way.
THE REST DAY card (Tuning.csv rest_day_cost), hanging just under the board. Only there while somebody is asleep.
THE REST BAR: one Mass mug per fixture of a sleeper's rest, on the floor in front of his bed. A FULL mug for every fixture he has slept. Scale is for both mugs.
An EMPTY mug for every fixture still to sleep. He plays again when every mug is full.
THE LUGGAGE TAG that shows a sleeper's name and power (and a price list over the key). It stretches to fit its words.
Where a message (bought, not enough money ...) shows for a few seconds, top-left, as a share of the screen.
